## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best wind direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.
- No survey or peer-reviewed study of the bottom was found.

| Swell direction | High | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Swell size | Moderate | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a surf magazine; 1 disagrees. |
| Swell period | Moderate | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Wind | Moderate | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Tide | Low | Supported by one source (a forecast site's spot guide); 1 disagrees. |
| Bottom / bathymetry | Moderate | Described by 4 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |
| Season | High | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| How the wave breaks | High | Described by 4 independent sources, including a surf magazine. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Seven publishers. Wikipedia, Surf-Forecast (Rincon and Bowl pages), WSL (two posts), SURFER (Surf Spot Mechanics, 2026, republished on Yahoo), SLS Beachsafe and Yeeew were read directly. Surfer Today (403) is kept as web_search. Biggest gain: SURFER's 2026 Surf Spot Mechanics piece. It gives an ideal swell direction of 196-215 deg (window 196-224) and a period of 15-16 s or longer, the first numeric period for Bells. It also gives a straight-offshore NW wind, with W-NW ideal and N-NE a 'devil wind'; a head-high to triple-overhead size; an April-September storm season; and an offshore ridge that refracts swell onto a gradually rising rock reef. Wind: NW from Surf-Forecast (two pages) and SURFER, all 15 deg from the profile's 300. Tide depends on the section. Surf-Forecast's templated line says mid on the rise (consistent with low_to_mid). SURFER says low for the Bowl and high for Rincon. Surfer Today (search evidence) says almost any tide. The profile's low_to_mid fits the Bowl. Size: Anderson's 3-4 to 10-12 ft Bowl (scale not stated), SURFER's head high to triple overhead and Yeeew's 'classic at six to eight foot (double to triple overhead)' are roughly consistent with 3-15. Yeeew's own conversion shows that local Victorian feet are about half the face height. SLS Beachsafe says it handles 1.5-7 m (up to about 23 ft), above the profile's maximum. Season: April-September (SURFER), April (WSL), March-October (Surfer Today), summer flat (Surf-Forecast); all consistent with March-September. Not found: a peer-reviewed reef study or an official wave description. The Bells Beach Coastal and Marine Management Plan PDF on marineandcoasts.vic.gov.au returned 403. The Surf Coast Shire PDFs and the Bells Wikipedia article say nothing about the waves. The Victorian Heritage Database link did not respond. WannaSurf's Australia index pages returned empty, so no WannaSurf Bells page was reached. Source type: SLS Beachsafe is run by Surf Life Saving Australia, a national lifesaving organisation, not a government agency, so it is classed community here. Its beach texts read like a coastal beach inventory; the project lead may want to reclassify it.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 3–4 ft [S4] · 4.9 ft [S8] | conflicting | S4, S8 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | head high to triple overhead | documented | S7 | no separate setting; working range 3–15 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 10–12 ft [S4] · 23 ft [S8] | conflicting | S4, S8 | `wave_height_max_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: Anderson's board advice (WSL) covers a 3-4 ft Bowl and Beachsafe says it handles waves from 1.5 m (1.5 x 3.28 = 4.9 ft); neither says whether these are face or offshore heights, and Anderson's is a surfed size rather than a stated limit.
  - S4 (World Surf League): “Anderson recommends everything from a small-wave groveler for Rincon to a board that could handle 3-to-4 foot up to 10-to-12 foot Bowl.”
  - S8 (Surf Life Saving Australia (Beachsafe)): “It can handle anything from 1.5 up to 7 m.”
- **Ideal range**: SURFER gives the best surf size as head high to triple overhead, a face height relative to the surfer; it gives no number in feet.
  - S7 (SURFER (republished on Yahoo)): “Surf Size: Head-high to triple overhead”
- **Maximum suitable**: Anderson's board advice runs up to a 10-12 ft Bowl, while Beachsafe says it handles up to 7 m (7 x 3.28 = 23 ft); neither states the scale (face or offshore), and Anderson's figure is a board range rather than a stated limit.
  - S4 (World Surf League): “Anderson recommends everything from a small-wave groveler for Rincon to a board that could handle 3-to-4 foot up to 10-to-12 foot Bowl.”
  - S8 (Surf Life Saving Australia (Beachsafe)): “It can handle anything from 1.5 up to 7 m.”

### Swell direction

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ideal bearing | 196–225° (SSW to SW, clockwise) | documented | S2, S3, S4, S7 | `optimal_swell_direction` 195–230° (SSW to SW, clockwise) |
| Acceptable range | — | not documented | — | `swell_window` 160–250° (SSE to WSW, clockwise) |
| Blocked directions | — | not documented | — | no separate setting (outside `swell_window`) |
| Exposure | exposed reef and point break; Rincon, the top section, picks up the most swell | documented | S2, S9 | no setting |

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: SURFER gives 196-215 deg as the ideal direction for shape and Surf-Forecast (Bells and the Bowl) gives southwest (225 deg); the value spans both, and WSL adds that Bells is a demanding venue when the swell pulses from the southwest.
  - S7 (SURFER (republished on Yahoo)): “The ideal swell direction for shape falls between 215° and 196°.”
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the optimum swell angle is from the southwest.”
  - S3 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Clean groundswells prevail and the best swell direction is from the southwest.”
  - S4 (World Surf League): “When the swell is pulsing out of the southwest, Bells is a demanding venue.”
- **Acceptable range**: No excerpt states a working window beyond the ideal direction (the window 196-224 appears only in the researcher's claim text, not in an excerpt).
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names swell directions that are blocked or shadowed by land or reefs.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls Bells an exposed reef and point break, and Yeeew says Rincon picks up more swell than the other sections and is therefore popular on smaller days.
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Bells Beach in Torquay is an exposed reef and point break”
  - S9 (Yeeew!): “The wave has three sections. Rincon, at the top, picks up more swell than the other sections, and is therefore popular on smaller days.”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: Anderson's board advice (WSL) covers a 3-4 ft Bowl and Beachsafe says it handles waves from 1.5 m (1.5 x 3.28 = 4.9 ft); neither says whether these are face or offshore heights, and Anderson's is a surfed size rather than a stated limit.
- **Swell height · maximum suitable**: Anderson's board advice runs up to a 10-12 ft Bowl, while Beachsafe says it handles up to 7 m (7 x 3.28 = 23 ft); neither states the scale (face or offshore), and Anderson's figure is a board range rather than a stated limit.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast (the same templated sentence on two pages) says best around mid tide, SURFER says low for the Bowl and high for Rincon, and Surfer Today (search summary) reports one source saying almost any tide.
